summary: Deliver per-event signed audit envelope + QRadar/SFTP ingest spec for external privacy assessor
description:
Issue summary: Customer requires a forensics-grade, per-event signed audit export for a third-party privacy assessment. They want each audit event wrapped in an immutable envelope with an ECDSA-P256 signature, monotonic per-tenant sequence number, and a manifest for batch verification. The export must be consumable by QRadar (they will test via an SFTP drop), include field-level mapping, and an integrity manifest.

Impact: External assessor cannot complete privacy attestation without cryptographically verifiable event-level evidence. Customer reports delayed audit engagement and potential contractual deadlines.

Environment: Redwood production audit pipeline for Aegis Health Systems (enterprise account) in us-east-1.

Acceptance criteria:
- Producer: Each audit event in the export is contained in a JSON envelope with the following canonical fields: envelope_id, tenant_id, seq_num, ts_utc, payload_type, payload (base64-utf8), signature (base64, ECDSA-P256 with SHA256), signer_key_id, signer_key_pem_metadata.
- Manifest: For each batch file (hourly), a manifest.json provides file_hash (sha256), file_size_bytes, event_count and a batch_signature signed with the same key family.
- Delivery: Hourly SFTP drop (FTPS optional) to customer-provided host with TLS, filename pattern: aegis_audit_us-east-YYYYMMDD-HH.jsonl.gzip and a .manifest.json alongside it.
- SIEM mapping: Provide QRadar mapping file (CSV) mapping Redwood canonical fields -> QRadar event properties, plus a short ingestion guide (sample log line and ingestion pipeline).
- Verification doc: Short runbook with commands to verify signatures using openssl/ecdsa utilities and to validate manifest file.

Requested timeline: Customer asks for a validated sample within 5 business days and production-ready configuration within 3 weeks.

Attachments: Customer provided sample event schema and assessor checklist in initial support email.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - request for export/spec, not a system bug. For validation we will produce a sample export and provide steps to validate signatures against published signer_key_pem_metadata.
logs: Relevant pipelines: audit-ingest-service v2.4, export-worker v1.9. No 5xx errors observed in last 24h. Example pipeline trace: trace-id 6f8a-20260310-ef12 shown in internal dashboard link.

investigation_notes: Prototype approach: sign at export-worker using ephemeral signing key retrieved from KMS HSM. Payload is the canonicalized JSON of the audit event (sorted keys, UTF-8), then base64-encoded into payload field. Compute signature over 'tenant_id|seq_num|ts_utc|payload' using ECDSA-P256-SHA256.
Edge case: Large payloads (>64KB) are chunked. Proposed approach: include content_sha256 in envelope and compute signature over content_sha256 instead of inline payload when chunked.
Preservation: Store signer_key_id and signer_key_rotation_index in manifest and publish ephemeral public key in signer_key_pem_metadata so assessor can verify past batches.

Compliance note: Must ensure PII redaction options are honored. Customer confirmed they want HIPAA-relevant fields pseudonymized before export; support to coordinate with Customer Success to confirm pseudonymization config.

QRadar mapping: QRadar expects 'payload' field decoded into 'raw_event' or mapped into 'extensions' depending on parsing pipeline. We will provide two example DSM rules: one that decodes base64 to raw_event and one that routes fields into QID fields.
resolution: In progress: sample produced and delivered. Next steps: finalize manifest schema, publish signer_key_pem_metadata and rotation history, prepare QRadar CSV mapping and Splunk HEC example, and obtain written confirmation of pseudonymization settings from customer. Target: production export config by 2026-03-31.
resolution_notes: If production rollout approved by customer, schedule a ticket to add per-tenant export configuration in console with encryption-at-rest and optional PII pseudonymization toggle. Follow-on task INT-40202 will implement automated nightly verification jobs for signed batches.
workaround: Interim: deliver signed sample batches on request via secure S3 presigned link with separate checksum file and manual signature verification instructions. This avoids SFTP setup delays.
